items.case: signing.nk and signing.pub are both missing
items.text:
error: signing.nk and signing.pub are missing from <dir>
hint: mashctl init --config <file>
items.note: From ctl #1390. The signing refusals print in the specification's error rule: `error: <what>` then `hint: <command>`, on stderr, exit 1. <dir> is the key folder as the error carries it (the plain path). The public keys the earlier text printed are not in default output. They are left out of --json too: the error object has only `error` and `hint`, and cliframe has no detail slot for errors. Printed by every mashctl command that signs (endpoint create, reissue, delete) and by init for the first two cases.

items.where: mashctl, a global option before the verb
items.note: mashctl accepts global options before the verb, as mash does (today: error: unknown command "--json"). The result is exactly that of mashctl status --json. The rule "Options go anywhere after the tool's name" already says so; the code does not yet.

items.where: mash and mashctl, a flag that does not exist
items.note: An unknown flag is reported as an unknown flag, in both tools, wherever it stands (today mashctl says unknown command "--verbose", and mash says "unknown option --x" after a command or "mash has no command --x" before it). No hint (ADR 0168): a hint is a command that fixes the problem, and no command fixes a flag that does not exist. Exit 2, nothing attempted.

items.where: mash --help (the top of the tool's help)
items.text:
Trusted mail between agents. Speaks as one endpoint.

SAP is the Synadia Agent Protocol, NATS is the message server mash
talks to, and creds are the file that signs an endpoint in to it.

Everyday:
  mash send <address> [<message>] [options]    Send a message to an endpoint.
  mash inbox [options]                         List the messages this endpoint
                                               has received.
  mash read <number>                           Show one message in full.
  mash who [<prefix>] [options]                List the endpoints you can see,
                                               and which are online.
  mash status                                  Say in one line whether mail
                                               works for this endpoint, and
                                               whether it is online.
  mash doctor [options]                        Check everything mail depends on
                                               for this endpoint, and say how to
                                               fix what is wrong. Changes
                                               nothing.
  mash version                                 Print the version. It can also be
                                               run as --version.

Setup:
  mash join <file> [options]                   Install an endpoint's credentials
                                               on this machine from a join file.
  mash key create [options]                    Make your own key pair, for when
                                               the seed must never leave this
                                               machine.

Integration:
  mash serve [options]                         Run as an MCP server for an agent
                                               host. Started by the host, not by
                                               hand.
  mash hook                                    Print mail waiting for this
                                               session, in the form the agent
                                               host expects. Run by the host
                                               after each tool call and with
                                               each prompt.

Raw SAP:
  mash prompt <address> <text>                 Ask an endpoint a live question
                                               and wait for its answer. Not
                                               stored: if the recipient is not
                                               there, it fails.

Global options:
  --endpoint <address>  Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Not
                        needed for the everyday and setup commands when only one
                        is installed here. mash serve and mash hook always need
                        it said: a session becomes an endpoint only because
                        someone chose that.
  --creds <path>        The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                        folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>        The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>           The certificate authority's certificate, when the server
                        uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>   The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  --detail              Print the fuller answer: after the usual line, more as
                        'label: value' lines; with --json, the fuller object.
  --json                Print the result as JSON: the same object the matching
                        MCP tool returns.
  --no-color            Never use color. Color is used only on a terminal, and
                        NO_COLOR is honored.
  -h, --help            Show help for the command.

An endpoint is addressed owner.group.name: MASH_ENDPOINT (or config.json
"endpoint", or --endpoint). With none set, the one endpoint whose creds file
(owner.group.name.creds, mode 0600) is in the config directory is used; with
several, name one.
A global option may stand anywhere in the command. A flag beats its environment
variable, which beats config.json.
Configuration: config.json {"servers","endpoint","ca"} in $MASH_CONFIG_DIR
(default ~/.config/mash, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mash), overridden by MASH_SERVER
(commas between several), MASH_ENDPOINT, MASH_CA, MASH_CREDS, MASH_ADMIN_CREDS,
MASH_HOST (see docs/install.md).
State (spool, hook.log): $MASH_STATE_DIR (default $XDG_STATE_HOME/mash, else
~/.local/state/mash).
Slow link: "open_timeout" (default 20s) and "call_timeout" (default 15s), or
MASH_OPEN_TIMEOUT and MASH_CALL_TIMEOUT.
Also tunable: lease_retry, transient_budget, transient_max, cli_timeout,
admin_timeout (MASH_LEASE_RETRY, MASH_TRANSIENT_BUDGET, MASH_TRANSIENT_MAX,
MASH_CLI_TIMEOUT, MASH_ADMIN_TIMEOUT).
items.note: Only the three lines after the first are new: one sentence that says what SAP, NATS and creds are, in the top-level help of both tools and nowhere else. The rest is today's help, unchanged. Same sentence in mashctl --help.

items.text:
usage: mashctl <verb> [args]

SAP is the Synadia Agent Protocol, NATS is the message server mash
talks to, and creds are the file that signs an endpoint in to it.

  mashctl init --config path [--dry-run] [--json]
      set mash up on a NATS server you already have, from a setup file; safe to
      run again
  mashctl status [--json]
      one line per server: whether it works, how many endpoints it has, how many
      are online
  mashctl limits show [--json]
      print the limits in force
  mashctl doctor [--strict] [--json]
      check the server, mash's storage on it and every endpoint's records, and
      say how to fix what is wrong; changes nothing
  mashctl limits apply [prefix] [--dry-run] [--json]
      raise existing inboxes to the configured limits (never lowers); prefix is
      an owner, owner.group or one address
  mashctl endpoint list [prefix] [--wide] [--json]
      the endpoints in the directory
  mashctl endpoint show ADDRESS [--json]
      one endpoint: its state, labels and public key
  mashctl endpoint create ADDRESS [--out PATH] [--public-key PATH] [--dry-run]
          [--json]
      make an endpoint and its credentials, for example acme.demo.bob
  mashctl endpoint reissue ADDRESS [--out PATH] [--public-key PATH] [--dry-run]
          [--json]
      give an endpoint new credentials and cancel the old ones
  mashctl endpoint delete ADDRESS [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
      revoke the endpoint's user key, remove its record and inbox, burn the
      address, rename its creds file
  mashctl endpoint set ADDRESS key=value... [--dry-run] [--json]
      set role, description, host, capability or label.NAME
  mashctl endpoint unset ADDRESS key... [--dry-run]
      remove those values
  mashctl endpoint suspend ADDRESS
      refuse new mail to an endpoint; its stored mail and credentials stay
  mashctl endpoint resume ADDRESS
      take new mail again, undoing suspend
  mashctl endpoint inbox ADDRESS [--after number] [--limit n] [--json]
      what is in an endpoint's inbox, without any message text
  mashctl endpoint permissions ADDRESS
      the NATS permissions an endpoint's user needs
  mashctl version [--json]
      print the version and the commit

Global options (before or after the verb):
  --server <url>       The server address. May be given more than once.
  --creds <path>       The administrator's creds file.
  --ca <path>          The certificate authority's certificate, when the
                       server uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>  The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  --detail             Print the fuller answer: after the usual line, more as
                       'label: value' lines; with --json, the fuller object.
  --json               Print the result as JSON.
  --no-color           Never use color.
  -h, --help           Show help for the command.
items.note: Four changes and nothing else. (1) The same one-sentence explanation of SAP, NATS and creds as mash --help. (2) A Global options block (the options the specification lists for mashctl, said to work before or after the verb). (3) --json is listed for endpoint list, show, set and inbox, as it is for the other verbs. (4) resume has the one description it has in endpoint --help. Today the block and the four --json flags are missing and resume reads "undo suspend" here and "take new mail again" in endpoint --help.

items.text:
usage: mashctl endpoint <command> [args]
commands:
  list [prefix] [--wide]      list the endpoints
  show <address>              show one endpoint
  create <address> ...        make an endpoint and its credentials
  reissue <address> ...       give an endpoint new credentials
  delete <address> ...        remove an endpoint
  set <address> key=value...  set role, description, host, capability, labels
  unset <address> key...      remove those values
  suspend <address>           refuse new mail to an endpoint
  resume <address>            take new mail again, undoing suspend
  inbox <address>             list what is in an inbox, without the text
  permissions <address>       print the NATS permissions an endpoint needs
Run mashctl endpoint <command> --help for a command's options.
items.note: Only the resume line changes: the one description of resume, the same as in mashctl --help. The specification's own description of resume ("Undo suspend.") changes to it, so mashctl endpoint resume --help says the same (today "take new mail again" here and "undo suspend" in mashctl --help).

rules_next.detail: Always an object, never a bare array: a list is {"endpoints": [...]}. It is the same object the matching MCP tool returns as its structured result. Field names are the glossary's words. Both are produced by one implementation. One policy in both tools: it is indented when standard output is a terminal and one compact line when standard output is a pipe or a file, as gh and aws do. An error object follows the same policy. The specification shows the indented form.

rules_next.rule: In --json, one name for one fact
rules_next.detail: A yes-or-no fact has one name in every command of both tools: online is a boolean wherever it appears (mash who, mash status, mashctl endpoint list and show, mashctl status), never ready, ok or state for the same fact; an endpoint's suspended state is its own boolean, suspended. ready stays the name of "mail works for this endpoint" and "the server works" (mash status and mashctl status, which was ok). A count is named as a count: endpoint_count, online_count, wake_count. An unset field is null: never "" and never left out, so a command's keys are the same on every run. An empty list is [] and an empty map is {}. A list's key is plural: capabilities, not capability. A doctor row's state (ok, warn, fail, skip) is a different fact and keeps its name.

rules_next.rule: A list is a plain table
rules_next.detail: A header row in capitals, two spaces between columns, no borders. Every cell is printed on every row, so a line stands on its own and can be grepped or cut: a repeated owner or group is not left blank. A sender or an endpoint is always its full address. --wide adds columns. An empty list is one sentence.
rules_next.replaces: A list is a plain table

rules_next.detail: Past tense, naming the thing, with a capital first letter and no full stop, in both tools: 'Created endpoint acme.demo.bob', 'Deleted endpoint acme.demo.bob', 'Mail sent (number 42)'. It does not print what another command already shows; it does print an identifier the person can get nowhere else, and the location of a file it wrote ('Credentials: <path>').

rules_next.rule: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines
rules_next.detail: The labels are the JSON field names. In every block of such lines, in text and under --detail, the labels are padded to the longest label in the block plus one space, so the values start in one column, and no value begins before it.
rules_next.replaces: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines

rules_next.rule: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint
rules_next.detail: A missing argument: 'error: mash send needs <address>'. A bad value: 'error: --kind must be one of blocker, question, task, result, fyi' or 'error: --reply-to must be a whole number'. Two things that cannot go together: 'error: mash send takes the message text or --file, not both'. A command that does not exist: 'error: unknown command "nope"', in both tools. A flag that does not exist: 'error: unknown flag --x', in both tools, wherever it stands, with no hint (ADR 0168: a hint is a command that fixes the problem, or there is none). Where there is a hint it is a command that fixes the problem, not a pointer to --help. Exit 2, and nothing is attempted.
rules_next.replaces: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint

rules_next.detail: 'error: no <thing> <value>', echoing the value as typed: 'error: no endpoint acme.demo.dave', 'error: no message 9'. The hint, when there is one, is the command that lists what exists or makes it.

rules_next.rule: --help has one layout, generated from this specification
rules_next.detail: For a command, in this order: the one-line description; 'Usage:' and the synopsis; 'Examples:'; 'Arguments:'; 'Options:'; 'Global options:'. Nothing else, 80 columns. For the tool itself: its one-line description, then one sentence that says what SAP, NATS and creds are (here and in no other help), then one heading per group in the specification's order ('Everyday:', 'Setup:', 'Integration:', 'Raw SAP:' for mash; 'Mesh:', 'Endpoints:', 'Owners:' for mashctl) with each command and its one-line description indented beneath, then 'Global options:' in both tools. A command is described once, in the specification, and that one description is used wherever the command is listed. Help is never written by hand beside the specification.
